attributes.body:
風（ふう） is a suffix that is used in Japanese to convey the meaning of 'in the style of (A)', or 'in the fashion of (A)'. Literally, this translates to 'in the wind of (A)', which is just the Japanese way of expressing the former statements.

To use 風（ふう）, attach it to the end of a noun that you want to label something as being in the 'style' of.

の may also be attached to the end of 風（ふう）, before connecting it to another noun. This will show that '(B) is in the style of (A)'.

Caution

As a compound structure, this suffix is always pronounced ふう, never かぜ (the standard reading of 風（かぜ）).

風 (ふう) and みたいに・みたいな both express resemblance or appearance. 風 attaches directly to nouns, e.g. アメリカ風料理 'American-style food' and can sound more formal. みたいな also attaches to nouns, but is more casual and makes a more straightforward comparison, e.g. ハンバーガーみたいな料理 = 'food like a hamburger'.

風 (ふう) and 的 (てき) are suffixes that turn nouns into descriptors. 風 suggests a style or 'air,' and is more limited in use, e.g. 日本風 or 和風 'Japanese-style'. 的 is broader, used for both adjectives and adverbs, e.g. 感情的 'emotional' and 定期的に 'regularly'.

風 and らしい② both express resemblance but differ in nuance. 風 means something has the 'air' or appearance of a type, e.g. 日本風建築 'Japanese-style architecture'. らしい② implies it embodies the ideal of that category, e.g. 日本らしい建築 implies 'quintessential Japanese architecture'.

attributes.body: Both describe style or appearance, but with different nuance. 型 refers to a concrete type, model, or category, e.g. 新型のスマホ ('A new model of smartphone') 風 suggests resemblance or outward style, often subjective or superficial, e.g. 昔風の家 ('A house in the old-fashioned style')

attributes.body: 風 (ふう) and ように・ような both express resemblance. 風 attaches directly to nouns, e.g. アメリカ風料理 'American-style food', while ような requires の before nouns, e.g. ハンバーガーのような料理 'food like a hamburger'. 風 often has a more stylistic nuance, while ような is a more neutral comparison.
